sites.functional_impact_measured: IP-1 formation assay in KNRK cells stimulated with trypsin and 2-furoyl-LIGRLO-NH2: PAR2 N-FLAG/C-HA11 showed similar potency and efficacy to PAR2-muGFP (EC50 trypsin 5.4×10⁻⁸ M, EC50 2F 7.8×10⁻⁸ M), confirming functional equivalence of the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: PAR2 is a GPCR with a signal peptide (residues 1–25); the mature extracellular N-terminus begins at residue 26 (I). An N-terminal FLAG on the full-length receptor can only reside at this single extracellular terminus — upstream is cleaved with the SP, and all other termini are intracellular or transmembrane. Python confirms residue 25 = T (last SP residue) and residue 26 = I (first mature residue), with TM1 beginning at residue 76, leaving 50 residues of extracellular space. The combined N-FLAG/C-HA11 construct was functionally validated by IP-1 assay with similar potency and efficacy to the reference PAR2-muGFP construct. L3 reports full-length, membrane-anchored PAR2 expressed in KNRK cells bearing an N-terminal FLAG epitope and a C-terminal HA11 epitope. The N-terminal FLAG must reside after the signal-peptide cleavage site (after residue 25, the last SP residue) because any tag upstream of residue 26 would be co-translationally cleaved. No specific junction residue is named in the paper; the position is derived from the single extracellular N-terminus of the mature protein.

sources.claim: To verify functionality of PAR 2 -muGFP, we compared signaling of PAR 2 -muGFP and PAR 2 with N-terminal FLAG and C-terminal HA11 epitopes transiently expressed in KNRK cells, which express low levels of PAR 2 and have been used extensively to study PAR 2 functions ( 13 ).

literature_notes: Ledger lines L1, L2, L4–L8 all concern the PAR2-muGFP C-terminal fusion and its functional/in-vivo validation. The C-terminus of PAR2 (residues 348–397) is intracellular per the authoritative topology landmarks; accordingly, the C-terminal muGFP and C-terminal HA11 tags are recorded in other_positions as intracellular, not surface sites. L3 is the only ledger line that mentions an extracellular tag (N-terminal FLAG), and it qualifies as a surface site. No ledger line reports any insertion in ECL1 (134–145), ECL2 (213–238), or ECL3 (314–324), so no internal loop sites are proposed. The N-terminal FLAG position is topology_derived because the paper names the tag orientation ('N-terminal') but not a specific junction residue; however, exactly one extracellular terminus exists (after SP cleavage at residue 25), making the junction unambiguous.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal muGFP fusion to full-length PAR2; the C-terminus (residues 348–397) is intracellular per topology landmarks — tolerated and functionally validated in vivo but not a surface tag site.
C-terminal HA11 epitope on the N-FLAG/C-HA11 PAR2 construct expressed in KNRK cells; intracellular C-terminus, tolerated with preserved IP-1 signalling but not accessible on the extracellular face.
